additions.english: saqmunya when you need to evacuate bile. In that case, you must mix it with something that opposes it in quality but agrees with it in purging, such as halilaj . To correct a dyscrasia that occurs later in those with tumors in the viscera, their diarrhea may weaken them; if you are forced to do so, use things like ivy and safflower for them. As for the purgative and khiyar shanbar , Hippocrates said: "Whoever has a stomach that is easily moved to vomit, the first step in their purification is to use vomiting in summer or spring when the time is right." This rids the body of fatigue. Know that if the person drinking it is accustomed to a loose stool or is not accustomed to vomiting, they should avoid it in times when it is not needed. It is necessary to prepare before diarrhea by thinning the humor one wishes to evacuate and widening the passages at that time, as this rids the body of fatigue. Know that the one who drinks it—if they are accustomed to a loose stool or are not accustomed to vomiting—should [use] one of the reducing regimens before using a strong medicine. Diarrhea with abdominal flaccidity is difficult and tiring. A purgative medicine may act as a laxative if the stomach is strong, if taken during extreme hunger, or if the person is accustomed to a loose stool, or if the medicine is heavier in essence than in speed of descent. The purgative may remain, causing trouble due to the weakness of the stomach, extreme heaviness, or because the medicine irritates it, or the person has indigestion. Every purgative medicine, if it does not purge the undigested humor, stirs up the humor it is meant to purge and spreads it throughout the body, dominating the body and attracting other humors to it, increasing that humor in the body. Among the humors, some are quicker to respond to vomiting, such as bile. Some are resistant to vomiting, such as black bile. Some have a condition like milk and stars ; its diarrhea is safer in itself. Whoever has a humor flowing downward, such as those with intestinal slippage, the gripping of the intestines hinders the purgative medicine. That which is composed of medicines that are strongly different during the time of diarrhea causes the diarrhea to become agitated; the first will purge the second before the second can purge, and perhaps the first will purge the very same second. In general, if a medicine evacuates the waste, there will be no agitation with it. If it is taken with agitation, then either it is evacuating what is not waste, or if the evacuated humor changes through vomiting or diarrhea to another humor, it indicates the purification of the body from the humor intended to be evacuated.

additions.english:
The proclamation of the Sayyid of the Malak of Tirmidh, that whoever goes to Samarkand in three or four days, for a certain task, [will receive] a robe, horse, slave, and slave girl, and several [pieces of] gold and silver; and the hearing of this proclamation by the clown in the village, and the buffoon coming to the King, saying: "I can go; this task is not [for me]."

The Sayyid of Tirmidh, who was the king there,
Had a task and important business in Samarkand,
He made a proclamation: "Whoever [can get there] in five days,"
The clown in the village heard that,
Two mounts died on that road,
Then he ran and saw [it] from the struggle.

The jester, he was an aware clown,
He searched for a city to become that oppression,
I brought news from there, treasures together,
He sat and ran until he was weary,
From [the] two, the horse became [spent] from that path,
At an untimely time, he sought the road and the king's court.

The Sayyid of Tirmidh, who was the king there,
Until the interior of Samarkand fell into confusion,
He found, he made a cry: "Five days,"
The clown in the village heard this order,
He made two mounts perish on that road,
He entered, crazy with the dust of the road.

The buffoonery of the clown was aware,
He sought a place, he was that oppressed one,
From there he brings news, I will be kind,
He made an effort and clamor on the road,
With the speed of travel, that shore remained,
The king at an untimely hour intended to arrive.

contradictions.source: 戰死則無武故不資以妾
contradictions.english: Dying in battle means no martial pride, therefore they are not provided with a concubine.
contradictions.why: The source text says 'no martial [rites/honor]', but the translation interprets 'wu' as 'martial pride' and links it to the lack of concubines, which is a misreading of the classical context regarding burial rites.

contradictions.source: 胎者之屢無為愛之皆無

contradictions.why: The translation misinterprets the classical structure '胎者之屢' (the frequent/repeated nature of the fetus/womb) as 'those who have a fetus', changing the subject of the sentence.
